script: "I spent 13 years hiding from my reality, and it nearly destroyed me...". I Ruined My Life, Don't Do the Same, Don't Give Up Okay, so I am going to tell you a story, and I know it's going to sound super relatable, but literally, I am 30-something, and I've basically ruined my life. I mean, I know we all make mistakes, but this is on a whole 'nother level, bestie. Growing up, high school was a mess for me. I wasn't exactly bullied, but I was that kid who got ignored, you know? People just didn't really want to hang out with me. And it didn't help that my parents were, like, nonexistent. Our house was always a war zone, with fights and screaming going down almost every week. No wonder I had low self-esteem, bruh. I was basically a lost teenager with no direction. The only thing that kept me grounded was gaming. I was addicted, and my parents were just like, "Yeah, sure, do what you want." They were clueless, too. I mean, I was dropping out of high school at this point, and I just figured, why bother? I felt like the world didn't want me, and I was stuck in this perpetual state of sadness. I thought to myself, "Why even try?" But then, I somehow managed to finish high school with an exam. Like, who does that? Not me, that's for sure. Fast forward to when I got my two degrees... Yeah, that was a joke. I was so convinced that I didn't have anything to offer the world. I thought, "Why even bother with a job or relationships? I'll just end up alone and miserable, anyway." The spiral of video games, snacking, and excessive media consumption started. It's hard to explain, but it's like, I was stuck in this never-ending cycle, and I couldn't find a way out. Honestly, I know it's not easy to hear, but if you're someone who's going through this, there is hope. My parents could've done things differently, but they didn't. However, I am hoping that by sharing my story, I can prevent someone else from making the same mistakes I did. Let me tell you, it's rough being me. I am stuck in a minimum-wage online job, living with my parents, and trying to delay my aging by any means necessary. It's a sad existence, bestie. I look at my reflection, and it hits me hard – I've missed out on so much. Dating? Forget about it. Fun experiences? Not a chance. And the worst part is, I am still stuck in my teenager's mindset while the rest of the world has moved on. It's not exactly my parents' fault; they were clueless, but still... It's hard to watch yourself age, and I've got to accept that my window of opportunity has passed. If you're someone who's reading this and you know someone who's going through the same thing, please, please tell them that they're not alone.
